claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins in a high-temperature disordered BCC state.
An isothermal hold near 700–800 °C is near the alloy's ordering temperature.
Slow cooling with a 700–800 °C hold permits local B2-like atomic ordering in the BCC matrix.
The B2-like ordered regions act as precursors or nucleation sites for secondary phases during subsequent thermal exposure.
Slower cooling and an intermediate-temperature hold provide sufficient atomic mobility for short-range chemical ordering.
B2-like ordered domains alter the local free-energy landscape.
Rapid quenching suppresses ordering and preserves a comparatively disordered BCC state.
Rapid quenching produces a different subsequent phase-transformation pathway from slow cooling with an intermediate hold.
Slow-cooled specimens with an intermediate hold will exhibit B2 superlattice reflections.
Secondary phases will appear during the subsequent 600 °C hold in specimens that developed B2-like ordering.
Rapidly quenched specimens will lack detectable B2-ordering signatures.
Rapidly quenched specimens will lack the subsequent phase changes predicted for the slow-cooled specimens.
Atomic diffusion below 600 °C is too limited to enable the proposed ordering.
Comparing rapid quenching with slow cooling plus an isothermal hold decouples ordering kinetics from purely diffusional effects.
